sources.researchNote: Commons gives only its upload date. The back of the card carries the writer’s date, “Hamborn am 7.10.20”, a Hamborn postmark of the same day and a 30-pfennig stamp, the postcard rate of 1920, so the card had been published by then. The view shows the town, not the hall of the 1929 concert, which the review does not name.

media.title: Hamborn, Rathaus — postcard posted in 1920
media.description: Picture postcard “Hamborn. Partie am Rathaus”, showing the town hall of Hamborn with its clock tower. The card was written and postmarked at Hamborn on 7 October 1920 and carries a 30-pfennig Germania stamp. Hamborn was then an independent town; it was joined to Duisburg in 1929.
media.altText: Tinted postcard of a gabled town hall with a tall clock tower at sunset, with trees, a cyclist and pedestrians in the square in front.
media.publicCaption: The town hall at Hamborn, on a postcard posted there in October 1920.
media.publicCreditLine: Postcard, publisher and photographer unidentified; Zeno.org; via Wikimedia Commons.
media.rightsNote: Public domain. The card names no photographer and was published by 1920, when it was posted at Hamborn; the German term for an anonymous work, seventy years from publication, had therefore run out before 1 January 1996, so the URAA restored nothing, and a work published before 1931 is in any case out of copyright in the United States.

places.publicNote: Hamborn, in the Ruhr area, was the setting of the ERKLA concert reviewed in December 1929. The review named Kaper alongside Giuliano Pomeranz, then performing as Julian Pomeranc, Alexander Zakin and Leopold Mittmann.
